title: Bundle script fallback fonts for CJK, Indic and Arabic coverage
body:
## Context
Every one of the 17 looks binds its display/body typeface from a twelve-family Latin set — Newsreader, Karla, Manrope, Bricolage Grotesque, DM Sans, Space Grotesk, Playfair Display, Nunito, IBM Plex Mono, Syne, Rubik, Archivo (`docs/design/design-system.md` §2 "Font stacks (F)" and §4). **None of them contains a single Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Gurmukhi, Odia, CJK or Arabic glyph**, so the moment we ship Hindi, Japanese or Arabic every string renders as tofu boxes. PRD-CO-374 in `docs/product/prd-04-sharing-collaboration-ai-study-a11y-i18n.md` §9 requires "full CJK + Indic glyph coverage" with line-breaking tested, and `docs/research/sources/accessibility-i18n-and-inclusive-design.md` §11 ("CJK & complex-text input") states the same. This is also the *only* i18n defect the pseudo-locale gate ({{SN-I18N-004}}) can surface but not fix, because that gate pads strings with Greek/Cyrillic/Indic glyphs precisely to expose missing coverage. The app must work offline (locked decision 3), so fallbacks are bundled assets — `design-system.md` §8 already requires the look fonts to "resolve offline". Flutter web/CanvasKit makes this urgent: CanvasKit does **not** silently fall back to installed system fonts the way the browser does for DOM text, so an un-declared script is guaranteed tofu on web.

## Scope
**In:** choose one fallback family per script — Noto Sans Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Gurmukhi, Oriya; Noto Sans CJK SC / TC / JP / KR; Noto Naskh Arabic (all SIL OFL, matching the licence posture of the look fonts); register them as `fontFamilyFallback` on the `SaneText` type scale so the look's Latin family always wins for Latin runs and the script font only fills gaps; subset/compress and enforce a download-size budget; on web emit `@font-face` with `unicode-range` so a visitor only downloads the ranges they actually render; ship CJK as an on-demand/deferred asset where the platform supports it (Play Asset Delivery / web deferred load) rather than in the base install; a tofu-detector test; licence + attribution rows in the About/licences screen and the release SBOM.
**Out:** the look font registration itself (design-system epic), the dyslexia reading fonts OpenDyslexic/Lexend (accessibility epic {{SN-A11Y-001}}), handwritten ink (vector strokes, not text), and PDF-embedded fonts (owned by {{SN-PDF-001}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A sample sentence in each of Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Odia, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Arabic renders with **zero `.notdef`/tofu glyphs** in every one of the 17 looks, light and dark.
- [ ] Latin text is unchanged: a look's display/body family still renders Latin runs (golden diff against the pre-change baseline is empty for `en`).
- [ ] Bundled font payload adds **≤ 12 MB** to the base Android download and **≤ 12 MB** to the iOS install after subsetting/compression; CJK faces beyond the user's locale are delivered on demand, and CI fails if the budget is exceeded.
- [ ] On web, the first paint of the English app downloads **no** script font; loading a Hindi page fetches only the Devanagari range; cached cold start stays < 3 s (locked decision 7).
- [ ] Mixed-script text in one paragraph (e.g. `Physics II — तरंगें (波)`) shapes correctly with no baseline jump > 1 px and no clipped ascenders/descenders at Display XL (38/1.08) and Body (14/1.45) from `design-system.md` §3.
- [ ] A font that fails to load degrades to the platform system font and logs a warning containing only the family name and script tag — never text content.
- [ ] Text still scales to 200 % and honours the 1.4.12 spacing overrides with the fallback family active (no clipping).

## Technical notes
Implement in `packages/sane_ui`: extend the `SaneText` widget and the resolved `fd`/`fb` families from the token `ThemeExtension` ({{SN-DS-002}}) to always append a script-fallback list via `TextStyle.fontFamilyFallback`. Assets live under `packages/sane_ui/assets/fonts/` and are declared in `packages/sane_ui/pubspec.yaml`; `sane_ui` stays a pure leaf (`docs/architecture/overview.md` §5) so no model/feature package is imported. For web, follow `docs/platform/web.md` and [ADR-0010](docs/adr/0010-web-pwa-strategy.md): CanvasKit resolves fonts from the declared asset manifest only, so every fallback must be declared; use deferred loading keyed off the resolved locale from {{SN-I18N-003}}. Prefer variable/static subsets over full faces; script fonts carry no italic — synthesise nothing, let the shaper handle it. Fallback order matters: put the look family first, then the script font for the active locale, then the remaining scripts, so a shared CJK codepoint resolves to the user's own regional variant (the classic Han-unification trap — `zh-Hans` must not render with the JP face). Implements PRD-CO-374.

## Security & privacy
- **Egress / tracking:** fetching fonts from a third-party CDN (Google Fonts et al.) would be an undeclared network egress and would leak the user's IP, locale and referer to a third party on every launch. Fonts are therefore **bundled, or fetched only from our own signed asset bundle over TLS 1.2+ with a hash check** — no new egress without an ADR + threat-model row (CLAUDE.md §7.4; MASVS-NETWORK-1, MASVS-PRIVACY-2).
- **Untrusted binary parsing:** font files are a historical memory-safety surface. We never write a parser; shaping goes through the platform/Skia stack, and downloaded packs are integrity-verified before registration (MASVS-CODE-4).
- **Resource exhaustion:** on-demand font downloads are size-capped and disk-quota-checked before write, and are cancellable, so a hostile or broken CDN response cannot fill the device (CWE-400).
- **Supply chain / licensing:** every face is SIL OFL, recorded with its version and licence in the SBOM and the in-app licences screen (MASVS-CODE-3).
- Baseline: no note content, ink coordinates, or PII in logs — font diagnostics log family names and script tags only.

## UX notes
The fallback must feel deliberate, not accidental. Per `docs/design/design-system.md` §3 the type scale (Display XL/L/M/S, Body, Body strong, Muted, Label, Mono) is fixed and only the *family* swaps per look — keep every size, weight, line-height and tracking when the script font takes over, so vertical rhythm is preserved even though an Indic or CJK heading cannot carry a look's serif personality (Paper, Editorial, Skeuomorphism). Verify the tightest looks first (Brutalism, Neo-Brutalism, Editorial, Y2K) where taller Devanagari ascenders and Arabic descenders are most likely to clip, and verify glass looks (Glassmorphism, Neumorphism, Claymorphism) keep contrast with heavier script strokes. States: while a deferred web font is loading, render with the system fallback rather than blank text (no FOIT); on failure, show the text, never a tofu box. a11y: substitution must not change announced text; targets stay ≥ 44 pt (iPadOS) / 48 dp (Android) / 24 CSS px (web); contrast tokens are unchanged.

## Test plan
- Golden: `packages/sane_ui/test/golden/i18n/script_coverage_test.dart` — one sample sentence per script rendered at Display S and Body in every look, light and dark (17 × 2 goldens per script sample set).
- Unit: `packages/sane_ui/test/fonts/tofu_detector_test.dart` — paints each sample string and asserts no codepoint maps to `.notdef` for the resolved fallback chain; also asserts `zh-Hans` and `zh-Hant` resolve to different faces.
- Unit: `packages/sane_ui/test/fonts/font_fallback_order_test.dart` — Latin runs keep the look family.
- Infra: `tools/scripts/check_font_budget.mjs` in CI fails the build over budget.
- Integration: `app/integration_test/web_font_deferred_test.dart` — English first paint fetches no script font.
- Manual: run on Chrome desktop, Safari iPadOS and a mid-range Android tablet in Hindi, Japanese and Arabic.

## Dependencies
{{SN-I18N-003}} (resolved locale drives which faces load), {{SN-DS-002}} (token `ThemeExtension` exposing the per-look `fd`/`fb` families). Coordinates with {{SN-DS-001}} for asset registration conventions.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, golden, font-budget gate, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed — font fallback strategy recorded in `docs/design/design-system.md` and `docs/platform/web.md`
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Support platform IMEs and complex-text editing in every text field
body:
## Context
Half of Sane Notes' locked locales cannot be typed without an input method editor: Chinese (Pinyin/Zhuyin), Japanese (Kana→Kanji conversion) and Korean (Hangul jamo composition) all commit text through multi-keystroke *composition* sessions, and Indic scripts compose multi-codepoint grapheme clusters (conjuncts like `क्षि`) that must move, select and delete as single units. PRD-CO-374 in `docs/product/prd-04-sharing-collaboration-ai-study-a11y-i18n.md` §9 requires platform IMEs to work "in all fields without intercepting composition events", and `docs/research/sources/accessibility-i18n-and-inclusive-design.md` §11 ("CJK & complex-text input") names the same three IME families plus line-breaking as the risk. The trap for a pen-first app is that our editor is full of raw key handling — keyboard shortcuts (`docs/design/gestures-and-shortcuts.md`), a lasso/tool state machine, and a text tool — and any of those swallowing Enter, Escape, Space or arrow keys during an active composition will corrupt or silently drop the user's input. This issue makes every typed surface IME-correct before the text tool ships in M2 (`docs/roadmap.md` M2 "Typed text tool + rich text").

## Scope
**In:** audit and fix every typed surface — the typed-text object in the editor, notebook/page titles and rename dialogs, the search field and "Ask my notes" input, tags, comment composer, invite-by-email, and settings fields; guarantee composition (`TextInputClient` / `composing` range) is never intercepted by shortcut handling; grapheme-cluster-correct caret movement, selection extension, and backspace/delete using `characters`; correct line-breaking for CJK (no inter-word spaces) and non-breaking within Indic clusters; IME candidate-window placement not obscured by the palette dock or overlays; interplay with Apple Scribble (`plugins/sane_scribble`) so handwriting-into-field and IME composition do not fight; keyboard-cache suppression on secret fields.
**Out:** the rich-text model and typed-text rendering itself ({{SN-TXT-001}}), handwriting recognition of Indic/CJK ink ({{SN-I18N-010}}), script font coverage ({{SN-I18N-008}}), and the on-screen ink-to-text conversion UX ({{SN-HWR-001}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Typing `ni hao` → selecting a candidate → Enter in the typed-text block, the notebook title, the search field and the comment composer commits `你好` exactly once, with the pre-commit composing text visibly underlined and **not** persisted to the document model until commit.
- [ ] A committed IME session is **one** undo step, not one step per keystroke (verified against the undo model {{SN-ED-001}}).
- [ ] While a composition is active, Enter/Escape/Space/arrow keys reach the IME and are **not** consumed by editor shortcuts or the tool state machine; pressing Escape cancels the composition and returns focus, with no keyboard trap (WCAG 2.1.2).
- [ ] Backspace over `क्षि` deletes one grapheme cluster; backspace over a ZWJ emoji family (`👨‍👩‍👧`) deletes the whole cluster; left/right arrow and shift-selection move by grapheme cluster, never by code unit.
- [ ] A CJK paragraph wraps without splitting inside a run of Latin/number text, and an Indic paragraph never breaks inside a conjunct cluster.
- [ ] The IME candidate window is never covered by the palette dock, page rail, audio bar or an overlay in any dock position (Bottom/Top/Left/Right, design Settings §12 `dock`).
- [ ] Secret fields (passphrase, recovery code, OTP) set `autocorrect: false` and `enableSuggestions: false` so the platform keyboard does not learn or cache them.
- [ ] All of the above pass on iPadOS, Android and Chrome/Safari web (Flutter web text-input path), and on a phone-width layout (~400 px).

## Technical notes
Work spans `app/lib/` text surfaces and the text primitives in `packages/sane_ui` (`SaneTextField` from the design-system component set) plus the typed-text editing path in `packages/sane_core`'s rich-text CRDT ([ADR-0005](docs/adr/0005-document-model-and-crdt.md); Peritext/Yjs-style per CLAUDE.md §2.4). Key rules: never mutate the document model from the *composing* range — only from `TextEditingValue` commits, otherwise a CRDT op is emitted per keystroke and sync/undo both degrade. Route shortcut handling through Flutter's `Shortcuts`/`Actions` with a guard on `TextEditingValue.composing.isValid` so the editor's key handlers stand down during composition; the editor canvas uses a raw `Listener` for pointers (CLAUDE.md §8) but keyboard must go through the focus system so IME wins. Use `package:characters` (`String.characters`) for every caret/selection/delete operation — never `String.length` or `substring` on code units. For Scribble, `plugins/sane_scribble` (see [ADR-0012](docs/adr/0012-native-plugin-strategy.md)) must relinquish the input connection before an IME session starts. Implements PRD-CO-374; complements the locale resolution in {{SN-I18N-003}}.

## Security & privacy
- **Keyboard caching of secrets (MASVS-PLATFORM-3, MASVS-PRIVACY-3):** third-party IMEs receive every keystroke and many sync learned text to their own cloud. Passphrase, recovery-code and OTP fields must disable autocorrect/suggestions and use an appropriate `keyboardType`/`obscureText` so the platform does not persist them; this matches the `LEAK` requirements in PRD-03 and the clipboard/screenshot-protection posture.
- **Untrusted input (CWE-20):** committed IME text is untrusted like any other text — validate length and normalise (NFC) before it enters the document model or the FTS index, and never build a query string by concatenation.
- **Bidi / homoglyph spoofing:** text arriving from an IME or paste may carry bidi control characters; reuse the sanitiser from {{SN-I18N-007}} when rendering it in chrome (comment previews, search snippets) so it cannot visually spoof UI (MASVS-PLATFORM-2).
- Baseline: no note content or keystrokes in logs — IME diagnostics log only state transitions and the active locale tag.

## UX notes
The composing run renders with the platform's underline convention using design tokens (`--ac` accent underline, `docs/design/design-system.md` §4 palette keys) rather than a hard-coded colour, so it reads correctly in all 17 looks and in dark mode. Candidate-window collision is a real risk in this design: the palette dock floats over the canvas and is dockable to any edge (design §7.3 and Settings §12 "Toolbar position"), so the text caret must scroll into a safe area when an IME opens, exactly as it does for the software keyboard. Empty/error states: if the platform reports no input connection (web without focus), show the field's placeholder and do not swallow keystrokes. a11y: composition changes are announced via `SemanticsService.announce` so VoiceOver/TalkBack users hear candidate commits; focus order and the 44 pt / 48 dp / 24 CSS px target minima are unchanged; on web every field stays keyboard-reachable with a visible focus ring (≥ 2 px, ≥ 3:1).

## Test plan
- Widget: `app/test/text/ime_composition_test.dart` — simulate `TextInputClient.updateEditingValue` with composing ranges for Pinyin, Kana→Kanji and Hangul; assert one commit, one undo step, and no model writes during composition.
- Unit: `app/test/l10n/grapheme_cluster_test.dart` — caret movement, selection and delete across Devanagari conjuncts, Tamil clusters and ZWJ emoji.
- Unit: `app/test/text/line_break_test.dart` — CJK and Indic wrapping cases.
- Widget: `app/test/text/shortcut_composition_guard_test.dart` — Enter/Escape are not consumed while composing.
- Integration: `app/integration_test/ime_fields_test.dart` — drive every typed surface on iPadOS/Android/web.
- Manual: real Pinyin, Kana and Hangul IMEs on device plus Apple Scribble into a text field.

## Dependencies
{{SN-I18N-003}} (supported locales + resolution), {{SN-TXT-001}} (typed text tool and rich-text model). Composes with {{SN-ED-001}} (undo grouping) and {{SN-I18N-007}} (bidi sanitisation).

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, integration, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed — the "no model writes from a composing range" rule added to `docs/architecture/document-model.md` and the shortcut guard to `docs/design/gestures-and-shortcuts.md`
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Build the handwriting-recognition language pack picker and downloads
body:
## Context
"English-only OCR" is gap #3 in `docs/research/sources/user-pain-points-and-market-gaps.md`: a Hindi- or Tamil-writing student cannot search their own notes in any major competitor. Sane Notes closes it. PRD-CO-373 in `docs/product/prd-04-sharing-collaboration-ai-study-a11y-i18n.md` §9 requires shippable on-demand recognisers for **Devanagari (Hindi, Marathi, Nepali, Sanskrit …), Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi/Gurmukhi and Odia** (the India priority set), plus **CJK** (`zh-Hani-CN`, `zh-Hani-HK`, `zh-Hani-TW`, `ja`, `ko`) and **Arabic-script** (`ar`, `fa`, `ur`), with the exact BCP-47 tags enumerated in `docs/research/sources/accessibility-i18n-and-inclusive-design.md` §11. [ADR-0016](docs/adr/0016-on-device-ml-and-ai.md) decision 8 fixes the delivery model: models download on demand, the user sees the size, integrity is verified, and a missing model degrades gracefully rather than crashing. `docs/roadmap.md` M3 makes it an exit criterion: "Recognition language is selectable per notebook and covers the broadest available set on **every** platform (no iOS-vs-Android disparity shipped)." This issue owns the *selection and delivery UX* layered on the recognition engine; the adapters themselves belong to {{SN-HWR-001}}.

## Scope
**In:** a `RecognitionLanguage` catalogue (BCP-47 tag, native + English display name, script, approximate pack size, per-backend availability); a per-notebook recognition-language setting plus an account-wide default in Settings → Handwriting & stylus (design §12); an optional **secondary** language for mixed-language pages; on-demand download with visible size, progress, pause/cancel and resume; honouring the existing `wifiOnly` preference (design Settings §12 "Hold audio and PDF uploads on mobile data"); a storage list showing installed packs with per-pack delete; graceful-absence behaviour (offer download or degrade — never silently recognise as English); an honest per-platform availability matrix surfaced in the UI, including the web fallback path where no on-device recogniser exists.
**Out:** the recogniser adapters, model lifecycle internals and the recognition index ({{SN-HWR-001}}); the custom per-user dictionary; cloud-recognition escalation and its consent banner; UI-language selection ({{SN-I18N-011}}); script font coverage for *displaying* the recognised text ({{SN-I18N-008}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Writing a Devanagari sentence, downloading the pack, then searching a word from it returns the page and scrolls to the matching ink — end to end, with the device in airplane mode after the download.
- [ ] The catalogue exposes at least the 9 India-priority Indic tags, `zh-Hani-CN`/`zh-Hani-HK`/`zh-Hani-TW`, `ja`, `ko`, `ar`, `fa`, `ur`, each with a native display name and a size shown **before** download starts.
- [ ] Selecting a language unavailable on the current backend shows an honest state ("Not available on this device — handwriting search for this language needs <platform>") and never falls back to English recognition silently.
- [ ] With `wifiOnly` on and the device on cellular, a download is blocked with a clear, actionable message and a "Download anyway" affordance; with Wi-Fi it proceeds.
- [ ] Download is cancellable and resumable; cancelling leaves **no** partial pack on disk; a corrupt or hash-mismatched pack is deleted and reported, never loaded.
- [ ] Deleting a pack frees at least the bytes it reported and the language reverts to the not-installed state; recognition previously derived from it is not deleted (the index survives).
- [ ] A page written in two scripts recognises both when a secondary language is set; with only one set, the unmatched script is left unrecognised rather than mis-transcribed.
- [ ] Per-notebook selection overrides the default and is persisted per profile; switching profiles switches the setting.
- [ ] Download and recognition never run on the UI isolate; starting a 40 MB download while inking keeps frames ≤ 16.7 ms (locked decision 7).

## Technical notes
The catalogue and selection state are pure Dart in `packages/sane_ml` (interfaces) with the concrete download path behind `plugins/sane_ml_native` (ML Kit `DigitalInkRecognitionModelIdentifier` / `RemoteModelManager` on Android and the Apple side per [ADR-0016](docs/adr/0016-on-device-ml-and-ai.md) §capability table, [ADR-0012](docs/adr/0012-native-plugin-strategy.md) for the federated plugin shape). Availability is resolved by **capability query, not platform check** (CLAUDE.md §8) so a device without a recogniser degrades identically everywhere. The per-notebook setting is a notebook-level LWW register in `packages/sane_core` ([ADR-0005](docs/adr/0005-document-model-and-crdt.md)) so it syncs; the account default is a profile preference alongside the {{SN-SET-001}} inventory. Pack files live in an app-private, path-confined model directory — never in a shared or world-readable location, and never inside the notebook blob store. Reuse the resolved UI locale from {{SN-I18N-003}} only as the *default suggestion*: recognition language is an independent choice (a student may write Hindi notes with an English UI). Implements PRD-CO-373 and the ADR-0016 graceful-absence rule.

## Security & privacy
- **Downloaded model = downloaded code/data (CWE-494, MASVS-CODE-4):** verify the publisher's signature/hash before a pack is registered or loaded; a mismatch deletes the file and surfaces an error. Never execute or `dlopen` anything fetched at runtime beyond the vendor SDK's own verified mechanism.
- **Transport (MASVS-NETWORK-1):** TLS 1.2+ only, no cleartext, no user-supplied URL — the download endpoint is fixed by the SDK/ADR and is the only new egress; it carries **only** a language tag and never ink, note content or an identifier (MASVS-PRIVACY-1, CLAUDE.md §7.1/§7.4).
- **Resource exhaustion (CWE-400):** cap pack size, check free disk before writing, stream to a temp file, and make cancellation atomic so a hostile/broken response cannot fill storage or leave partial state.
- **Path confinement (CWE-22, MASVS-STORAGE-2):** derive the on-disk pack path from a validated catalogue id, never from a server-supplied filename; the model directory is app-private and excluded from cloud backup.
- **No content leaves the device:** recognition itself is on-device by default (locked decision 6, design Settings §12 "Your ink never leaves the device to become searchable"); this issue must not introduce a path where selecting a language sends a sample stroke anywhere.
- Logging: language tags, pack ids and byte counts only — never ink coordinates or recognised text (CLAUDE.md §7.3).

## UX notes
New surface under Settings → **Handwriting & stylus** (design `docs/design/screens-and-flows.md` §12), which today holds Palm rejection / Pressure sensitivity / Draw with finger / Left-handed mode / Toolbar position / Double-tap the pencil — add a **"Recognition languages"** row that opens a list; the design sheet does not specify this row, so follow CLAUDE.md §9 and implement the decisive default with a `// DESIGN-OPEN:` comment linking `docs/design/screens-and-flows.md` §Open. Per-notebook override is reachable from the notebook `⋯` menu and the editor's recognition affordance. Rows show native name (in its own script — depends on {{SN-I18N-008}} or they will render as tofu), English name, size, and an install/delete control. States to design explicitly: **empty** ("No language packs yet — English works out of the box"), **downloading** (determinate progress + size + cancel), **offline** ("Downloading needs a connection"), **error/retry**, **unavailable on this device**, and **installed**. Renders across all 17 looks and dark mode using tokens only. a11y: rows ≥ 44 pt / 48 dp, progress announced with `SemanticsService.announce` ("Hindi pack, 40 percent"), each row's accessible name includes the English language name so a screen reader in any UI language can announce it, keyboard reachable on web with a visible focus ring.

## Test plan
- Unit: `packages/sane_ml/test/recognition_language_catalogue_test.dart` — every required BCP-47 tag present, per-backend availability matrix correct, native names non-empty.
- Unit: `packages/sane_ml/test/language_pack_manager_test.dart` — hash mismatch rejects and deletes; cancel leaves no partial file; disk-quota refusal; `wifiOnly` gating; path confinement rejects a traversal id.
- Widget: `app/test/i18n/recognition_language_picker_test.dart` — install/delete/unavailable/offline/error states.
- Golden: `app/test/golden/i18n/recognition_languages_test.dart` across representative looks, light + dark, and RTL.
- Integration: `app/integration_test/recognition_language_pack_test.dart` — write Devanagari, download, search offline.
- Perf: frame-time assertion while downloading during an inking session via `tools/perf_harness`.
- Manual: Android device (ML Kit packs) and iPadOS; confirm the availability matrix matches reality on each.

## Dependencies
{{SN-I18N-003}} (locale model and resolution), {{SN-HWR-001}} (recognition engine, adapters and model lifecycle), {{SN-SET-001}} (Settings surface and per-profile preference store), {{SN-I18N-008}} (script fonts, or native language names render as tofu).

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, integration, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed — the per-platform recogniser availability matrix recorded in `docs/platform/compatibility-matrix.md` and the new egress row added to `docs/security/threat-model.md`
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Add the Language & region picker to Settings
body:
## Context
A student in India routinely runs an English-language device while wanting a Hindi interface, and multilingual users switch deliberately rather than accepting the OS default — so the app needs its own language control, not just OS inheritance. PRD-CO-370 in `docs/product/prd-04-sharing-collaboration-ai-study-a11y-i18n.md` §9 requires that "switching locale changes all chrome" and that `zh-Hans`/`zh-Hant` are distinct choices; PRD-CO-377 requires that changing the UI language **never** touches note content. The design sheet (`docs/design/screens-and-flows.md` §12) currently has six Settings tabs — Account & plan, Sync & backup, Handwriting & stylus, Appearance, Notifications, Privacy & export — and **no language row**, so per CLAUDE.md §9 this issue implements the decisive default (a "Language & region" row under **Appearance**, next to Look and Dark mode, since both are presentation preferences) and leaves a `// DESIGN-OPEN:` comment linking `docs/design/screens-and-flows.md` §Open. This is the user-facing front end for the locale model built in {{SN-I18N-003}}.

## Scope
**In:** a "Language & region" row in Settings → Appearance opening a picker; a **"Use device language"** default that follows OS changes live; the supported-locale list rendered with native names (हिन्दी, 日本語, العربية, 中文（简体）/中文（繁體）) plus the English name as secondary text; separate region selection where it affects formatting (e.g. `en-IN` vs `en-US`) defaulting from the device; persistence as a per-profile preference through the {{SN-SET-001}} preference store; **instant** application with no restart, including live RTL flip; a "Partially translated" badge for any locale whose `untranslated.json` report is non-empty.
**Out:** the locale list and resolution logic itself ({{SN-I18N-003}}); RTL mirroring behaviour ({{SN-I18N-007}}); date/number/currency formatting ({{SN-I18N-005}}, {{SN-I18N-006}}); the *recognition* language picker, which is a different setting ({{SN-I18N-010}}); translation content ({{SN-I18N-012}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Selecting हिन्दी re-renders every piece of chrome in Hindi without an app restart, and the choice survives a cold start.
- [ ] Selecting العربية mirrors chrome immediately (dock, rail, nav, overlays) while the ink canvas and every stroke coordinate stay identical — verified by a canvas golden that is byte-identical before and after (PRD-CO-372/377).
- [ ] **"Use device language"** is the default; with it selected, changing the OS language while the app is backgrounded updates the app on resume; choosing an explicit language pins it and OS changes no longer apply.
- [ ] 中文（简体） and 中文（繁體） appear as separate rows and produce visibly different chrome.
- [ ] The preference is **per profile**: switching profiles switches the language, matching the multi-profile isolation rule in PRD-LB-350/PRD-PROF-004.
- [ ] Note content, notebook titles, tags and OCR transcripts are unchanged by a language switch (PRD-CO-377) — asserted by comparing the document model before/after.
- [ ] A locale with untranslated keys shows a "Partially translated" badge and falls back per-key to English rather than showing a blank or a raw key.
- [ ] Rows are ≥ 44 pt (iPadOS) / 48 dp (Android) / 24 CSS px (web), keyboard reachable on web with a visible focus ring, and each row's semantics label includes the English language name.
- [ ] Switching language does not drop the user's place: the currently open screen, scroll position and any open overlay survive the rebuild.

## Technical notes
Add the row to the Appearance tab built by the Settings epic ({{SN-SET-001}}) and store the value as a per-profile preference (LWW register, [ADR-0005](docs/adr/0005-document-model-and-crdt.md)) so it syncs with the profile rather than being device-local. Drive the app from a Riverpod provider holding `Locale?` (null = follow device) that feeds `MaterialApp.locale` ([ADR-0003](docs/adr/0003-state-management-and-app-structure.md)); the existing `localeListResolutionCallback` from {{SN-I18N-003}} still resolves the device case. Native display names come from the `SupportedLocale` model added in {{SN-I18N-003}}; do **not** hand-maintain a second list. The partially-translated badge reads the `untranslated-messages-file` report produced by the pipeline in {{SN-I18N-002}}, embedded at build time as a small generated const — never fetched at runtime. Files: `app/lib/settings/language_settings.dart`, provider in `app/lib/l10n/`. Implements PRD-CO-370 and PRD-CO-377.

## Security & privacy
- **Untrusted locale input (CWE-20, MASVS-PLATFORM-1):** a locale value arriving from a restored preference, a synced profile record, a deep link or an imported bundle is untrusted — validate it against `supportedLocales` before it reaches `MaterialApp.locale` or any `intl` formatter, and fall back to English on anything unrecognised. An arbitrary locale string must never flow into a format pattern or a file path.
- **Privacy (MASVS-PRIVACY-1):** the chosen language is a weak fingerprinting signal; it is stored locally/E2E-encrypted with the profile, never sent anywhere, and never attached to telemetry (telemetry is opt-in and content-free, [ADR-0011](docs/adr/0011-telemetry-and-diagnostics.md)).
- Baseline: no note content or PII in logs — log the BCP-47 tag only. The language switch must not write note content to any new location.

## UX notes
Surface: Settings → **Appearance** (design `docs/design/screens-and-flows.md` §12), directly under the 17-theme card grid and the Dark mode toggle, using the existing settings-row composite so it inherits every look. Copy in the product's calm, student-first voice (`docs/design/ux-principles.md`): title "Language & region", subtitle "Chrome and dates follow this. Your notes never change." — which also states PRD-CO-377 in-product. Ordering: "Use device language" first, then the best device match, then alphabetical by native name. Each row shows the native name as the primary label (needs {{SN-I18N-008}} fonts to avoid tofu) with the English name muted (`--mu`, Muted 12.5 per `design-system.md` §3). States: **selected** (check, accent `--ac`), **partially translated** (badge), **RTL preview** (the row's own text renders in its own direction). Must render correctly in all 17 looks, light and dark, at phone width (~400 px) and RTL. a11y: `Semantics` label "Hindi, हिन्दी, partially translated, selected"; `SemanticsService.announce` on change ("Language changed to Hindi"); the live rebuild must not steal focus.

## Test plan
- Widget: `app/test/settings/language_picker_test.dart` — list contents, selection persistence, "Use device language" behaviour, partially-translated badge, zh-Hans vs zh-Hant distinctness.
- Widget: `app/test/l10n/locale_switch_live_test.dart` — chrome rebuilds without restart; open overlay and scroll position survive.
- Unit: `app/test/l10n/locale_preference_validation_test.dart` — an invalid/unsupported stored or deep-linked locale falls back to English.
- Golden: `app/test/golden/i18n/language_settings_test.dart` across representative looks, light + dark, LTR + RTL.
- Integration: `app/integration_test/language_switch_test.dart` — switch to Arabic, assert chrome mirrors and a canvas golden is unchanged; switch profiles and assert the language follows the profile.
- Manual: change the OS language while backgrounded and resume.

## Dependencies
{{SN-I18N-003}} (supported-locale model and resolution), {{SN-SET-001}} (Settings surface, per-profile preference store). Renders correctly only once {{SN-I18N-008}} (script fonts) has landed; composes with {{SN-I18N-007}} (RTL mirroring).

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, integration, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed — the new Settings row recorded in `docs/design/screens-and-flows.md` §12 and the open design question noted
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Establish the translation workflow, glossary and linguistic QA gate
body:
## Context
The ARB pipeline ({{SN-I18N-002}}) gives us *slots* for translations; it does not give us translations, nor a way to keep them correct as the product changes. PRD-CO-371 makes an empty `untranslated-messages` report a release condition and PRD-04 §11.4 DoD item 4 makes the pseudo-locale gate plus real Indic coverage part of "done", so the project needs a repeatable path from "a new string landed in `app_en.arb`" to "that string is translated, reviewed and shipped in 18 locales" — with a hard gate that stops a half-translated or format-broken locale from reaching users. `docs/research/sources/accessibility-i18n-and-inclusive-design.md` §11 specifies the mechanical half (typed placeholders, ICU plurals/select, `untranslated-messages-file` tracking); this issue adds the human half: context for translators, a glossary of terms that must never be translated, a string-freeze rhythm, and automated validation of everything that comes back. Localisation is cross-cutting and audited in M7 (`docs/roadmap.md` M7 "i18n/RTL audit"), which is where this workflow must already be running.

## Scope
**In:** a written workflow in `docs/product/` or `docs/design/` covering string freeze per release, the export→translate→import loop, and who reviews what; export/import scripts (`tools/scripts/l10n_export.mjs`, `tools/scripts/l10n_import.mjs`) converting between ARB and the chosen vendor format; a mandatory `@description` (and `@placeholders` with `type`/`format`) for every message, enforced by a CI lint; a **glossary** of do-not-translate terms and of terms with a fixed translation; a **screenshot/context pack** so translators see where a string appears; automated validation of returned files (ICU syntax, placeholder set identity, no bidi control characters, no HTML/markup injection, length sanity); the release gate that fails when a release-blocking locale has untranslated keys; a linguistic QA checklist per locale.
**Out:** actually procuring translations (budget/vendor is a maintainer decision), the pseudo-locale gate itself ({{SN-I18N-004}}), store-listing and marketing copy translation (owned by {{SN-REL-001}} and {{SN-SITE-001}}), and user-content translation, which is an explicit Sage feature (PRD-CO-156, {{SN-AI-001}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `docs/` contains a translation-workflow document a new contributor can follow end to end without asking a question.
- [ ] CI fails if any message in `app_en.arb` lacks an `@description`, or if any placeholder lacks a declared `type` (and a `format` where it is a date/number/currency).
- [ ] `tools/scripts/l10n_export.mjs` produces a vendor-ready bundle containing **only** UI strings, their descriptions, placeholder metadata and screenshot references — a reviewer can diff it and confirm no note content, no user data, no keys/tokens.
- [ ] `tools/scripts/l10n_import.mjs` rejects a returned file that: changes the placeholder set of a message, breaks ICU plural/select syntax, introduces bidi control characters (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069), introduces raw HTML/markup where the source had none, or exceeds 300 % of the source length; each rejection names the message key and the reason.
- [ ] The glossary lists at least: **Sane Notes**, **Sane Sage**, `.sanenote`, `.sane`, **Pro**, **Free**, and the 17 look names, each marked translate / do-not-translate with a rationale.
- [ ] A release-blocking locale with a non-empty `untranslated.json` fails the release gate; a non-blocking locale warns instead, and the app shows its "Partially translated" badge ({{SN-I18N-011}}).
- [ ] Running the import on a deliberately corrupted fixture produces a non-zero exit and no partial write to `lib/l10n/`.
- [ ] The linguistic QA checklist exists per locale and covers terminology, tone (`docs/design/ux-principles.md`), truncation, and number/date correctness.

## Technical notes
Keep the source of truth in `app/lib/l10n/app_en.arb` and generated code out of translators' hands. The scripts are Node 22 ESM under `tools/scripts/`, matching the existing tooling convention (`scripts/validate-issues.mjs`, CLAUDE.md §11), and run in the same CI workflow as the other gates from {{SN-CI-001}}. Validation must compare the *placeholder set* (names and types) rather than string equality, since word order legitimately changes; ICU parsing can reuse the same `intl` message parser the generator uses so a file that imports cleanly is guaranteed to `gen-l10n` cleanly. Screenshots for context are generated from the golden-test harness rather than captured by hand, so they refresh automatically. **Maintainer decision required (`needs-decision`):** (a) which translation platform/vendor is used — a managed service (Crowdin/Lokalise-class), a community workflow, or machine translation with human review; and (b) which locales are release-blocking for v1 versus "ship partially translated with the badge". Implement the neutral default meanwhile: plain ARB round-trip on disk, English + Hindi + Arabic release-blocking (they are the locales that exercise Indic shaping and RTL), everything else non-blocking. Implements PRD-CO-371 and supports PRD-04 §11.4.

## Security & privacy
- **Third-party data exposure (MASVS-PRIVACY-4):** translators are outside the trust boundary. The export contains UI strings and metadata only — never note content, user names, emails, telemetry, or anything from a real user's device. The exporter enforces this structurally by reading only the template ARB, and the workflow doc states it as a rule; a threat-model row records the translator as an external actor.
- **Untrusted data returning into the build (OWASP-A08, integrity failures):** a translated ARB is input from outside the repo and is validated before merge — ICU syntax, placeholder identity, markup and length. An unvalidated translation can break a format string at runtime (CWE-134) or crash a screen in exactly one locale, which is a denial of service for those users.
- **Bidi / homoglyph spoofing (CWE-1007):** translated strings are rendered in security-relevant chrome (share roles, "data leaves device" indicator, permission dialogs); bidi overrides or confusable characters in a translation could misrepresent a security decision, so they are rejected at import.
- **No secrets in ARB (MASVS-CODE-3, CLAUDE.md §7.2):** the lint fails on anything resembling a key, token or URL with credentials in a message value.
- Baseline: no note content or PII in logs; the scripts log message keys and locale tags only.

## UX notes
No new runtime screen; the user-visible consequences are indirect but real. The glossary protects brand surfaces: `SaneSageMark` and the "Sane Sage" name are trademarked/fixed-colour per `docs/design/design-system.md` §1 and must never be localised, while the 17 look names (Paper, Skeuomorphism, Retro, Minimalism, Glassmorphism, Flat, Material, Bento UI, Pop, Maximalism, Y2K, Cyberpunk, Neumorphism, Claymorphism, Brutalism, Neo-Brutalism, Editorial) are decided once and applied consistently across the Appearance tab, onboarding and the marketing site. Tone guidance for translators comes from `docs/design/ux-principles.md` and the preserved microcopy in `docs/design/screens-and-flows.md` §16 — short, calm, second-person, never scolding. Where a translation cannot fit (German compounds, Tamil expansion), the checklist instructs the translator to shorten rather than let the UI truncate, and the pseudo-locale gate ({{SN-I18N-004}}) is the safety net. a11y: descriptions must also cover semantics-only strings (screen-reader labels, announcements) so those get translated too — they are invisible in screenshots and are the most commonly missed.

## Test plan
- Unit: `tools/scripts/test/l10n_import_test.mjs` — fixtures for placeholder mismatch, broken ICU plural, bidi control injection, markup injection, over-length, and a clean file; assert exit codes and that no partial write occurs.
- Unit: `tools/scripts/test/l10n_export_test.mjs` — export contains only allowed fields; a planted "secret" or content-like value fails the scan.
- CI: the `@description`/placeholder-metadata lint runs on every PR touching `app/lib/l10n/`; the release gate runs on release branches.
- Manual: run a full export → hand-translate five strings into Hindi and Arabic → import → `flutter gen-l10n` → app renders them.

## Dependencies
{{SN-I18N-002}} (ARB pipeline and `untranslated-messages-file`), {{SN-I18N-004}} (pseudo-locale gate is the layout safety net this workflow relies on), {{SN-CI-001}} (CI to host the lints and release gate). Blocked on a maintainer decision for the translation platform and the release-blocking locale set.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, ARB metadata lint, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed — the workflow document and glossary committed, and the translator recorded as an external actor in `docs/security/threat-model.md`
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Audit RTL and multilingual layout across locales, looks and devices
body:
## Context
`docs/roadmap.md` M7 makes it an exit criterion that "WCAG 2.2 AA met on all chrome; **every supported locale (incl. Arabic RTL) renders correctly**", and PRD-04 §11.4 DoD item 4 pairs the pseudo-locale gate with real end-to-end Devanagari plus one more Indic script. The automated gates we already have each cover one slice — {{SN-I18N-004}} catches truncation and mirroring against synthetic strings, {{SN-I18N-008}} catches missing glyphs, {{SN-I18N-007}} pins the canvas LTR — but none of them proves that the *real* translated product looks right on a real device, in a real look, at a real text size. This issue is the human-plus-harness audit that closes the loop before beta, producing a signed-off report and a reusable matrix rather than a one-off eyeball pass. It is deliberately scheduled in M7 alongside the accessibility audit, since the two share screens, devices and many failure modes (truncation, focus order, target size).

## Scope
**In:** define and run the audit matrix — supported locales × the key screens × representative looks × light/dark × device classes; a scripted capture harness built on the golden/integration infrastructure and `tools/device_lab`; automated checks over the captures (tofu/`.notdef` detection, overflow detection, mirrored-layout assertions for `ar`, digit-shape and date/number spot checks); a manual checklist for the things a machine cannot judge (does the Hindi heading read naturally at Display L, is the Arabic line-height comfortable, does the Japanese label break in a sensible place); filing and tracking the defects found; a written report in `docs/qa/` with pass/fail per cell and any accepted risks.
**Out:** fixing the defects (each becomes its own issue against the owning area), the WCAG/screen-reader audit ({{SN-A11Y-001}}), performance soak ({{SN-PERF-001}}), and the pentest.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The matrix covers at minimum: locales `en`, `hi`, `ta`, `bn`, `ar`, `ja`, `ko`, `zh-Hans`, `zh-Hant`, `de` (longest Latin expansion), `pt`; screens Login, Profiles, Onboarding, Library, Editor (all four dock positions), Templates overlay, Import PDF overlay, Share overlay, Search/Ask, Settings (all six tabs), Upgrade overlay (design `docs/design/screens-and-flows.md` §§3–13); looks — all 17 for at least one locale, and 5 representative looks (Paper, Minimalism, Glassmorphism, Brutalism, Editorial) for all locales; light + dark; device classes iPad (ProMotion), mid-range Android tablet, Chrome desktop web, iPhone, Android phone, and one foldable in both postures.
- [ ] **Zero** tofu glyphs across every capture (automated `.notdef` scan).
- [ ] **Zero** unresolved truncation/overflow defects at default text size, and none at 200 % text scaling on the screens WCAG 1.4.4 applies to.
- [ ] In `ar`, chrome mirrors on every captured screen while the canvas capture is pixel-identical to the `en` canvas capture (PRD-CO-372).
- [ ] Dates, numbers and ₹ prices are correct per locale in the captures (spot-checked against {{SN-I18N-005}} and {{SN-I18N-006}} expectations, including Indian lakh/crore grouping).
- [ ] Focus order in RTL follows visual order, and left-handed mode composed with `ar` does not double-flip the page rail (PRD-CO-337).
- [ ] Untrusted text containing bidi control characters, rendered into search snippets and comment previews, does not visually reorder surrounding UI (negative test).
- [ ] Every defect found is filed with a screenshot, locale, look, device and owning area; the report records pass/fail per cell and is signed off before M7 exit.
- [ ] The harness is re-runnable by a single command and its captures are diffable, so the audit is cheap to repeat each release.

## Technical notes
Build on the existing golden harness and `integration_test`/patrol setup from {{SN-QA-001}} rather than a new framework: a driver enumerates the matrix, forces `MaterialApp.locale` and the look, pumps each route, and writes a capture plus a metadata JSON (locale, look, theme, device, screen). Automated scans run over the captures in `tools/scripts/`: a `.notdef` scan (reusing the tofu detector from {{SN-I18N-008}}), an overflow scan (assert no `RenderFlex` overflow errors were recorded during the pump and no clipped text rects), and a mirroring assertion comparing `ar` captures against horizontally-flipped `en` captures for chrome regions only. Real devices come from `tools/device_lab` and `docs/platform/compatibility-matrix.md`; the web leg runs against Chrome desktop per `docs/platform/web.md`. Keep the canvas comparison separate from the chrome comparison so a legitimately-unmirrored canvas does not fail the mirroring check. Report lives in `docs/qa/i18n-rtl-audit-<release>.md`. Verifies PRD-CO-370/372/374/375/376 end to end.

## Security & privacy
- **Bidi spoofing of security-relevant chrome (CWE-1007, MASVS-PLATFORM-2):** the audit explicitly exercises attacker-controlled text — an imported or shared page title, an OCR transcript, a collaborator's comment — containing U+202A–U+202E / U+2066–U+2069, and asserts the sanitiser from {{SN-I18N-007}} prevents it from reordering or masking surrounding UI such as share-role labels or the "data leaves device" indicator.
- **Capture hygiene (MASVS-PRIVACY-1):** audit fixtures use synthetic notebooks only. No real user content, account, token or device identifier may appear in a capture committed to the repo or attached to a report; captures are reviewed before commit, and the device-lab accounts are test accounts.
- **No new egress:** the harness runs locally/in CI against local fixtures; it introduces no network call and therefore no threat-model change beyond the existing test infrastructure.
- Baseline: no note content or PII in logs; the harness logs locale/look/screen identifiers only.

## UX notes
The audit is judged against the design source of truth: `design/Sane Notes.dc.html` screen composition, `docs/design/screens-and-flows.md` §§3–13 for each surface, and `docs/design/design-system.md` §3 for the fixed type scale (Display XL 38/1.08 through Label 11/.08em) and §4 for the 17 looks. Expect the worst results in the tight, typographic looks (Brutalism, Neo-Brutalism, Editorial, Y2K) with the most expansive locales (German compounds, Tamil and Malayalam expansion) and in the glass looks (Glassmorphism, Neumorphism, Claymorphism) where heavier Indic and Arabic strokes can lose contrast over a frosted backdrop — the design's frosted-glass rule requires note contrast to be maintained. Empty, loading, error and offline states must be captured too, not just the happy path: they contain the longest sentences in the product and are the most commonly untranslated. a11y overlaps to verify in passing: 44 pt / 48 dp / 24 CSS px targets survive longer labels, focus rings stay visible (≥ 2 px, ≥ 3:1), and text at 200 % still reflows at 320 CSS px.

## Test plan
- Harness: `tools/scripts/i18n_audit.mjs` (matrix driver + scans) and `app/integration_test/i18n_audit_capture_test.dart` (capture driver).
- Automated scans: `app/test/golden/i18n/notdef_scan_test.dart`, `app/test/golden/i18n/rtl_mirror_scan_test.dart`, overflow assertions recorded during capture.
- Negative test: `app/test/l10n/bidi_spoofing_test.dart` — hostile titles/snippets cannot reorder chrome.
- Manual: the per-locale linguistic and layout checklist from {{SN-I18N-012}}, executed on the device-lab set, with a native or fluent reviewer for `hi` and `ar` at minimum.
- Output: `docs/qa/i18n-rtl-audit-<release>.md` with the pass/fail matrix and filed defect links.

## Dependencies
{{SN-I18N-007}} (RTL mirroring + bidi sanitisation), {{SN-I18N-008}} (script fonts, or every non-Latin cell fails on tofu), {{SN-I18N-011}} (language picker to drive the app into each locale), {{SN-QA-001}} (golden/integration harness), {{SN-PERF-004}} (device lab). Real translations from {{SN-I18N-012}} make the audit meaningful; without them it can still run against pseudo-locales.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, golden, integration, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed — audit report committed under `docs/qa/` and the M7 exit-criteria checklist in `docs/roadmap.md` ticked for i18n/RTL
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md
